messages:
maria: Proposing new GPU node pools in us-west-2. Plan: separate nodegroups for p4 (heavy inference) and g4 (smaller jobs). Prefer SPOT for cost, but keep a small ON_DEMAND reserve (desired_size=2) for long-running or critical batches. Will apply taints (nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule) and label nodes hardware=gpu. Anyone concerned about that approach?

tim: Sounds reasonable. Question: which instance sizes exactly? p4d vs p4de? g4dn.xlarge vs g4dn.12xlarge? Need to match scheduler resource requests.

maria: Thinking p4d.24xlarge for the heavy pool, g4dn.xlarge for the smaller pool. We'll tune later. Two nodegroups: gpu-p4-spot and gpu-g4-spot, plus gpu-reserve-on-demand (small).

ishaan: For TF/EKS: use capacity_type=SPOT on the large groups with a separate ON_DEMAND nodegroup for reserve. Example snippet: 
```
resource "aws_eks_node_group" "gpu_spot" {
  cluster_name    = var.cluster
  node_group_name = "gpu-spot"
  instance_types  = ["g4dn.xlarge", "p4d.24xlarge"]
  capacity_type   = "SPOT"
  launch_template { id = aws_launch_template.gpu.id }
}

resource "aws_eks_node_group" "gpu_reserve" {
  cluster_name    = var.cluster
  node_group_name = "gpu-reserve"
  instance_types  = ["g4dn.xlarge"]
  capacity_type   = "ON_DEMAND"
  desired_size    = 2
}
```
Also recommend mixedInstancesPolicy or managed nodegroup with multiple instance types to improve spot diversification.

vlad: Small infra notes: add node-labels = { hardware = "gpu" } and taint via bootstrap so pods don't land on GPU nodes by accident. Also run a Node Feature Discovery daemonset to annotate GPU compute capability, e.g., nvidia.com/gpu.compute=8.

maria: Agree. Also need secure image pulls and driver access to private ECR. I don't want to bake KMS keys into userdata.

ishaan: Don't bake keys. Give nodegroup IAM role permission to decrypt via KMS and read Secrets Manager. Use external-secrets or the AWS secrets CSI driver to populate k8s secrets. Example ExternalSecret: 
```
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: gpu-registry-creds
spec:
  secretStoreRef:
    name: aws-sm
  target:
    name: gpu-puller-creds
    template:
      type: kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson
  data:
    - secretKey: .dockerconfigjson
      remoteRef:
        key: /prod/ecr/gpu-puller
```
That way no KMS material in TF outputs.

tim: Make sure autoscaler knows about the pools. Add proper nodegroup annotations and use cluster-autoscaler flags like --nodes for each group and --balance-similar-node-groups. Also ensure the autoscaler has permissions to drain spot nodes cleanly.

maria: I've opened a draft TF PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3599 that adds launch templates, the two spot pools, the on-demand reserve, node labels/taints, and the IAM role for secrets. infra-ci-bot ran plan successfully.

infra-ci-bot: Plan successful - no destructive changes detected. (run-id: ci-20260320-19)

vlad: One more for scheduling: add node affinity/taints for model capability so schedulers can pick nodes with the right GPU compute SM. NFD will help with that. Also annotate whether the node has MIG slices if we enable MIG later.

ishaan: Also add a graceful fallback strategy: when spot interruptions happen, prefer draining spot and rescheduling pods to the reserve pool. Use a PDB and preStop hook to give pods time to checkpoint. We should also add a lifecycle hook on the ASG to delay termination until the pod is drained.

tim: Checklist for merge from me: explicit capacity_type per group, least-privileged IAM for secrets/ECR, autoscaler config, terraform state locking, and tests for node-labels/taints.

maria: Will update PR: set exact desired_size variables, add NFD DaemonSet manifest, add ExternalSecret example in docs, and include PDB + preStop hook. Aiming to merge after reviews and a final green CI. ETA EOD today. Thanks :thumbsup:
